Yalta in Shenzhen?

Richard Haass

In principle, the planned summit of the US, Russian, and Chinese presidents could usefully address what should be done to limit the proliferation of nuclear weapons, ensure that AI is more a force for good than harm, and end ongoing wars and prevent new ones. But principle is one thing; in practice, we are likely to see something else.

Doug Mills - Pool/Getty Images

Nov 17, 2026
5 min read

SHENZHEN—China’s technology hub is hosting the annual gathering of the 21 members of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC). But what is capturing the lion’s share of the world’s attention is something else: a planned three-way meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Russian and Chinese counterparts, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping.
